PullRequest.Title: sessions: keep sticky header attached during relayout
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes an intermittent blank Sessions header after the sidebar temporarily receives zero render height.

The treatment reuses one header DOM node between the normal tree row and the sticky row. When both virtualized templates were unavailable during relayout, disposal detached that shared node and could leave the fixed-height row empty.

This change:
- parks the shared header in its stable non-virtualized container instead of detaching it;
- restores it to the normal or sticky row when rendering resumes;
- preserves focused Find controls across DOM handoffs; and
- adds regression coverage for zero-height relayout and filtering focus.

Validation:
- `npm run compile`
- `npm run hygiene`
- targeted ESLint
- focused Sessions lifecycle tests

Scenarios.Scenario: Sessions sidebar temporarily lays out at zero height and later regains height
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SessionsList.layout synchronously updates the virtualized tree; disposal of the normal or sticky header template reparents the single shared header into the stable header container and invokes updateHeaderLayout before layout returns. Relayout later renders that same node back into the tree.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: DOM reparenting plus updateHeaderLayout; the desktop path writes display styles and may synchronously read clientWidth for the header row and label.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared header handoff per header-template disposal; cardinality is constant with respect to session count and the zero-height transition disposes at most the normal/sticky header instances.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The header was detached (or returned from sticky to the connected source row) during disposal and no layout callback ran from disposal; rendering still invoked the existing layout callback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously inside list layout and must complete before the zero-height or restored layout returns.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of zero-height/restore relayout transitions, not the number of sessions; effective header cardinality is one.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All tree disposal, DOM reparenting, focus restoration, and layout callbacks run serially on the renderer/UI thread; no queue, limiter, or parallel work is involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No data cache participates. The virtualized row/template cache can retain header templates, but the shared header DOM node is now parked in its stable owner rather than retained in a detached template.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the synchronous DOM handoff and callback path; repository code directly shows the callback's style writes and geometry reads.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser style/layout cost varies with sidebar complexity, but the changed work is bounded to one header node and a small fixed set of geometry/style operations per actual handoff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded synchronous work to preserve the shared header across a rare relayout transition, with no collection-scaled allocation or boundary fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scrolling the navigation treatment so the Sessions header becomes sticky or returns to its source row
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A scroll event updates sticky-scroll state. When the state materially changes, the sticky widget disposes its prior template, the changed renderer reparents the shared header and runs the layout callback, and a new sticky template may render and run the existing callback again before the state update completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reparent the header, optionally restore focus, and update responsive header visibility using DOM style writes/clientWidth reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one extra layout callback for the single shared Sessions header per sticky-template disposal. Equal sticky states avoid rerendering; work does not run once per session row or once per unchanged scroll event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Sticky disposal could return the header to its connected source and restore focus, while the subsequent render performed the sole header layout callback. The diff adds a disposal-side callback to cover parking in the stable container.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous on sticky-state transitions and therefore on those scroll updates, but fixed-size and limited to one header.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Material sticky-state transitions while scrolling, after state-equality suppression; one header regardless of session collection size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Scroll handling, sticky-state comparison, renderer disposal/rendering, DOM focus operations, and geometry reads are serialized on the UI thread. Unchanged sticky states are coalesced by StickyScrollState.equal; only changed states rerender.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Sticky state equality suppresses rebuilding for unchanged states. The row/template cache does not duplicate the shared header, and no warm/cold data cache changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the added disposal-side callback and sticky lifecycle. User-visible frame impact is not strongly evidenced because state equality bounds frequency and only one header is processed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of sticky-state transitions depends on scrolling and section structure; the per-transition incremental cost is a fixed header layout and is not session-cardinality-scaled.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Although the change can add one synchronous responsive-header layout on a sticky handoff, it is bounded, coalesced for unchanged scroll states, and insufficiently evidenced as a concrete user-visible regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Typing in Find while the header moves between normal, sticky, and parked containers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Find input events filter the tree; if filtering causes header template replacement, disposal captures the focused descendant, reparents the shared header, restores focus, and runs the layout callback before the filtered tree render completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: DOM focus restoration with preventScroll, header reparenting, and responsive-header style updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared header/input per template handoff caused by a filter update; not per matching session. When Find is open, updateHeaderLayout takes the early style-only branch and does not read clientWidth.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Focus was captured only in disposeElement and the header could be detached by disposeTemplate. The diff also captures focus during template disposal and parks the node instead of detaching it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before the filter render completes so focus remains usable; work is fixed-size for each actual handoff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Find keystrokes that materially replace the header template, after tree filtering/template reuse; effective DOM cardinality is one header and one focused input.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Input filtering and header lifecycle work are serialized on the UI thread. There is no external concurrency; the shared header ensures only one focused input node exists.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No network/data cache is involved. Tree filtering and template reuse are unchanged; only ownership of the one header DOM node changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the input-to-filter and header lifecycle path; low evidence of meaningful performance degradation because work is constant and primarily replaces detach/reattach operations needed for focus preservation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filter frequency follows keystrokes, but a handoff is required for the changed work and the Find-open callback avoids geometry reads, limiting cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance issue. The focus-preservation work is constant per actual handoff and does not fan out with session results.

Scenarios.Scenario: Constructing the Sessions list with or without an externally owned header
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SessionsList construction performs a constant-time option consistency check and creates either an empty renderer list or one SessionsHeaderRenderer before constructing the tree.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One operation per SessionsList instance; independent of session count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous single-threaded constructor work; no scheduling or parallelism.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the constructor diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the added check and zero/one-element array are fixed-size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. The additional startup work is constant and negligible, and the fixture-only option normalization does not affect product runtime.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and traced zero-height relayout, sticky scrolling, Find filtering/focus, and construction. The only new runtime cost is bounded DOM handoff/focus/layout work for one shared header; no collection-scaled repeated work, unbounded retention, expensive external boundary fan-out, or actionable user-visible regression was established.
